headline: Treasure Coast Weekly Traffic Report: I-95 ramp closures, overnight lane closures planned Sept. 5-11
teaser: Drivers across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties should expect a busy week of road work, including multiple I-95 ramp closures near Kanner Highway, High Meadow Avenue and Becker Road.
body:
Treasure Coast drivers should prepare for a busy week of construction-related lane and ramp closures beginning Tuesday, Sept. 8, with Florida Department of Transportation projects affecting I-95 and several major local roads in Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

The most significant impacts are expected along I-95, where overnight resurfacing work will close multiple lanes and ramps in Martin and St. Lucie counties. FDOT says schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Drivers can check [FL511](https://www.fl511.com/) for real-time interstate traffic information and [FDOT District 4](https://www.d4fdot.com/) for updated construction and lane-closure information.

## Martin County

On I-95 from Bridge Road north to the Martin-St. Lucie county line, two southbound lanes are scheduled to close from 7:30 p.m. to 5:30 a.m. Tuesday, Sept. 8, through Friday, Oct. 30. Two northbound lanes are scheduled to close from 8:30 p.m. to 6:30 a.m. over the same period for milling and resurfacing.

Several southbound ramps in the Palm City and Stuart area will also close overnight from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Tuesday, Sept. 8, through Thursday, Sept. 10. The affected ramps are the southbound I-95 exit to Kanner Highway at Exit 101, the southbound entrance ramp from Kanner Highway, the southbound exit to High Meadow Avenue at Exit 102 and the southbound entrance ramp from High Meadow Avenue. FDOT says only one ramp will be closed at a time, with signed detours in place.

The southbound I-95 exit to Bridge Road at Exit 96 is scheduled for a later closure from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Sept. 13, through Thursday, Sept. 17. Motorists will be directed to leave I-95 at Kanner Highway and use Pratt Whitney Road to reach Bridge Road.

Along A1A/NE Ocean Boulevard near Jensen Beach, northbound and southbound traffic between NE Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced by one lane intermittently Tuesday, Sept. 8, through Friday, Sept. 11. Two-way traffic will be maintained by flaggers while crews work on pavement widening and drainage.

SW Martin Highway between SW Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard will also have intermittent nighttime lane closures from 7 p.m. to 6 a.m. Tuesday through Thursday for milling and resurfacing.

## St. Lucie County

I-95 work will also affect Port St. Lucie drivers between Gatlin Boulevard and Becker Road. Two northbound lanes may close from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Tuesday, Sept. 8, through Friday, Sept. 11, while two southbound lanes may close from 7:30 p.m. to 5:30 a.m. during the same period. Lane shifts are possible.

Several Becker Road ramps will close on different nights. The southbound I-95 entrance ramp from Becker Road is scheduled to close from 7:30 p.m. to 5:30 a.m. Tuesday, Sept. 8. The northbound exit to Becker Road at Exit 114 is scheduled to close during those same overnight hours Tuesday and Wednesday, Sept. 8-9. The northbound entrance ramp from Becker Road is scheduled to close Thursday, Sept. 10, and again Sunday, Sept. 13.

Farther north, the northbound I-95 exit to Gatlin Boulevard and Tradition Parkway at Exit 118 is scheduled to close from 7:30 p.m. to 5:30 a.m. Monday and Tuesday, Sept. 14-15.

On Port St. Lucie Boulevard, one lane in each direction between SE Seafury Lane and SE Lennard Road may close intermittently from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Tuesday through Friday. Two lanes may close intermittently overnight from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. during the same period. U.S. 1 between SE Jennings Road and NW Golden Oak Trail will also have intermittent daytime and overnight lane closures for construction and repaving.

Drivers on SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard should expect one lane to close intermittently between SW Jordin Avenue and SW Alcantarra Boulevard from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Tuesday through Friday. FDOT also says extended closures may occur on portions of SW McCall Road, SW McHord Avenue, SW Paar Drive, SW Koler Avenue, SW McDevitt Avenue, SW McComb Avenue and SW McCoy Avenue while drainage and utility work is underway. Those closures may begin at 7 a.m. Tuesday and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, although adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time and access to homes and businesses will be maintained.

Near Fort Pierce, I-95 shoulder lanes between Glades Cut Off Road and just south of Okeechobee Road may close overnight Tuesday through Friday for guardrail and other work.

Construction also continues around the new A1A North Causeway bridge. The bicycle lanes and shared-use path on the north side remain closed, with pedestrians directed to the south-side sidewalk. Several nearby sections of U.S. 1, Old Dixie Highway, Juanita Avenue and Harbortown Drive continue to have weekday lane closures as work progresses.

## Indian River County

In Vero Beach, one lane on the eastbound and westbound 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive may remain closed as bridge rehabilitation work wraps up.

The Oslo Road interchange project continues to create some of the county's most significant traffic impacts. One lane in each direction on Oslo Road, from about 1,500 feet west of I-95 to SW 58th Avenue, is scheduled to remain closed around the clock through September. Nighttime lane closures are also possible on 66th Avenue, 74th Avenue, 82nd Avenue and 58th Avenue near Oslo Road. I-95 within the project limits may have as many as two lanes closed nightly from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m., Sunday through Thursday.

On S.R. 510/90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, northbound and southbound traffic may be reduced by one lane intermittently from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Tuesday, Sept. 8, through Friday, Sept. 11.

Drivers near Sebastian Inlet should also be aware of a major traffic shift planned for later in the month. FDOT expects northbound and southbound traffic on A1A/Jimmy Buffett Memorial Highway to shift onto temporary pavement beginning around 7 a.m. Thursday, Sept. 17, weather permitting. The temporary pattern is expected to remain in place through late 2028 while the new Sebastian Inlet bridge is built.

Sections of both the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park are also partially closed for the bridge project, although the park and remaining parking areas remain open.

FDOT's weekly Treasure Coast report covers construction activity from Sept. 4 through Sept. 11. Motorists traveling through active work zones should allow extra time, watch for changing traffic patterns and follow posted detour signs.
